body:
### Problem

There's no way to set a buffer-local directory. You can set window-local and tab-local directories with `:lcd` and `:tcd` respectively, but there's no `:bcd`. This makes working with multiple projects difficult unless you use tabs or a [vim-rooter](https://github.com/airblade/vim-rooter) style plugin.



### Expected behavior

Introduce a `:bcd` command that sets a buffer-local directory.

buffer-local directories and `vim.fs.root()` can potentially be used as a primitive for "projects"

Related: #8610 

P.S: Emacs has buffer-local directories, but not window-local or tab-local ones.

comment_data.body:
Given the discussion in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8610, it does seem like this could be a necessary feature. Need feedback from others.

Note also that a requirement is to have an ergonomic way to get the buffer's "current directory". At least via `getcwd()`, but also maybe a buffer-local option or variable? (Need to hear comments on that.)

How on earth would this work with the window local directory.

Sounds like local options but worse.

> How on earth would this work with the window local directory.

The same way tab-local directories work with window-local directories. The current hierarchy in vim is this:

1. window-local directories
2. tab-local directories
3. the global directory

window-local directories override tab-local directories, which override global directories.

A buffer-local directory will likely sit between window-local and tab-local directories. The new hierarchy would then be:

1. window-local directories
2. buffer-local directories
3. tab-local directories
4. the global directory
  
> Sounds like local options but worse.

I would've liked if vim exposed directories as an option but we have the `:cd`, `:tcd`, `:lcd` family of commands instead. Creating a `:bcd` command instead of a buffer-local option is more consistent with what vim already offers.

Aside from projects, directory browsers like `netrw` or [oil.nvim](https://github.com/stevearc/oil.nvim) could benefit from buffer-local directories. Doing `:e ~/somedir/` followed by, say, `:grep` or `:!touch` would run in `~/somedir/` as opposed to the global directory.
`netrw` can already use the window local directory which isn't hard to change when the buffer is changed. It would probably require the same amount of code as using the buffer local directory.

`netrw` is just given as an example; I'm not suggesting that we change it. But yes, you can emulate buffer-local directories with autocommands that `:cd` on `BufEnter`. That's what vim-rooter style plugins do.

> There's no way to set a buffer-local directory. [...] This makes working with multiple projects difficult unless [...]

The first sentence is not a problem, but a fact before adding `:bcd`. It would be great if you could elaborate more on how you work with multiple projects without tabs?

> Aside from projects, directory browsers like netrw or oil.nvim could benefit from buffer-local directories. Doing :e ~/somedir/ followed by, say, :grep or :!touch would run in ~/somedir/ as opposed to the global directory.

What's wrong with this, if you just want to stick to the directory of every buffer:

```vimscript
augroup Bcd
  au!
  au WinEnter * exe 'lcd' '%:p:h'
augroup END
```

to target a specific group of buffers by `let b:var`: (probably create a toggle for setting `b:var` to `0`/`1`)

```vimscript
augroup Bcd
  au!
  au WinEnter *
    \ if exists('b:bang_lcd') && b:bang_lcd
    \ | exe 'lcd' '%:p:h' |
    \ endif
augroup END
```

On the other hand, having `:cd`, `:tcd`, `:lcd` does _not_ immediately validate the existence of `:bcd`:

* `:cd` is like treating a group of tabpages as a viewport, which worths a persistent directory.
* `:tcd` is like treating a group of windows as a viewport, which worths a persistent directory.
* `:lcd` is like treating a single window as a viewport, which worths a persistent directory.
* `:bcd` is ... not related to a viewport.

Every directory of these viewports are **persistent** regardless of those buffers they're carrying. I'm not sure that we can generalize/extend the list with `:bcd` without more considerations.

Edit: add more arguments.

> Every directory of these viewports are **persistent** regardless of those buffers they're carrying.

LSP (and vim-fugitive, etc.) are strong hints that every buffer has a "root dir" that it cares about. The [examples mentioned here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/33320#issuecomment-2784195398) make sense.

`:terminal` buffers with OSC 7 handling also would benefit from a buffer-local CWD.

When setting a CWD with `:lcd`, creating a new window/tabpage inherits that CWD. Would be useful to be able to avoid that, via `:bcd` (which should *not* "inherit").

Vaguely related: From my config I have two user commands, `:InDir` and `:InRoot` that run an excmd in the "right" directory. 

`:InDir ~/projects/foo/ :grep xyz`

`:InRoot :grep func`

> It's my personal opinion that buffer-local directories should have less priority than window-local ones

hmm, now that I am using `:bcd` (for `:terminal` OSC 7), not sure I see the advantage of that @msaher . If I switch to a buffer with a buffer-local dir set, I expect that buffer's directory to take precedence.

what is your rationale?

> not sure I see the advantage of that

I said that because I viewed `:lcd` as a brute force option because it's visual (a window) and it's easy to undo (just close the window), but I don't have a strong opinion about it.  It's probably rare to mix `:lcd` with `:bcd` anyway (it can get confusing).

I'll need to play around with the new `:bcd` implementation before forming strong opinions.
k, LMK how it goes. it does seem simpler to do the "obvious" thing, where the precedence matches the scope hierarchy (buf < win < tab < global)
Decided to rearrange the scope precedence in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41194

Should `:terminal` inherit the buffer-local directory? What behavior do you expect here?

```
:cd $HOME
:e mybuf
:bcd /
:!pwd " shows / as expected
:term pwd " shows $HOME because its a different buffer. Expected?
```

@msaher that's addressed by `:help terminal-osc7` : https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/3a396466930f22d279934023e1459225a6de9389/runtime/doc/terminal.txt#L176-L187

The door is open for us to consider "automating" that somehow, but it's messy because it is shell-dependent.

@justinmk `:help terminal-osc7` is for `cd`ing in shells. This use case is for spawning a `:terminal` from a buffer in the "right" directory based on the buffer-local directory. It's a admittedly a less common thing to do and overlaps with `:help terminal-osc7`, but it's something that I wanted to point out.

My mistake; the behavior in your example is because `:bcd` is not "sticky" (no "inherit" behavior).

Maybe `:bcd` should be "sticky" after all.

The "sticky" behavior will be much less problematic once `:bcd!` / `:lcd!` / `:tcd!` are available, since there will be a way to opt-out:

```vim
:enew  " new window inherits local dir
:bcd!  " clear the local dir
```

We may also a way to clear ALL inherited local CWDs, perhaps `:cd!` (which currently does nothing useful).

actually we just need to fix `:terminal`: it should spawn with effective CWD when the command was invoked.

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41211

> actually we just need to fix :terminal

Agreed. But I think there are other cases where we want to "inherit" the buffer-local directory. For example, when using `:tj`:

```
$ ls bcd-example
hello.c  main.c  tags
$ nvim bcd-example/main.c

:bcd bcd-example
:tj say_hello " jumps to hello.c
```

Since `:bcd` is not sticky, `:tj say_hello` will open `hello.c` in the global CWD and some users might find that unintuitive. 

It seems there are cases where we want `:bcd` to be sticky. Are there cases where we don't want sticky behavior?

Also, if we make `:tj` inherit the buffer-local directory, what will happen if we do `:tj say_hello` and there's already a buffer named `hello.c`. Will it automatically open it and set its buffer-local directory? What if `hello.c` already has a buffer-local directory? Will it override it?

> Since `:bcd` is not sticky, `:tj say_hello` will open `hello.c` in the global CWD and some users might find that unintuitive.

Also when e.g. using a file-picker or `:find`. That is the current intended behavior, but I agree it's not what I expect when using a file-picker.

> What if `hello.c` already has a buffer-local directory? Will it override it?

No. But you've hinted at (one of?) the main frictions with buffer-dir inheritance: "opening" a buffer does not always imply a *new* buffer. Whereas "opening" a tab/win always implies a *new* tab/win.

> Also when e.g. using a file-picker or :find. That is the current intended behavior, but I agree it's not what I expect when using a file-picker.

Given that, should `:bcd` revert back to being sticky? As you said, with `:bcd!` it'll become less annoying.

> "opening" a buffer does not always imply a new buffer. Whereas "opening" a tab/win always implies a new tab/win

Yes! Great way to put it.

> should `:bcd` revert back to being sticky?

Need to collect use-cases: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41210
